label: rare: original-phase step after v and 3 in prefix, often first token f
explanation: Extremely sparse feature (0.004% of steps, about 1 activation per sequence where active), weak magnitude (max 0.22). About 80% of mass is in the original phase at t>=3, enriched near the end of the input (to_go 0-1, L=9). It shows a tendency to fire when the prefix contains v and/or 3 (often adjacent pairs like v v, 3 3, 3 v at positions 1-3) and the first token is f (18x lift; z and 0 also enriched). The current input is often 0, x, n, h, w, z. Never fires at t<3 and almost never in the copy phase or on the delimiter. But many steps that match these conditions do not fire. The best conjunction (first token f, v and 3 seen) reaches only ~7% precision and ~35% mass recall on dev, and stricter positional versions top out at F1 ~0.16. It looks like a rare conjunction of prefix-content features that no simple predicate captures.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=f (+4.36), phase=2 & in_tok=0 (+3.75), phase=2 & out_tok=f (+3.48), orig3=3 (+2.54), orig2=3 (+2.53), prev2_tok=v (+2.36). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-3.57), orig8=- (-2.36), prev3_tok=- (-2.09), L=9 & recall_idx=-1 (-1.69).
